Mobile UX · Event discovery

Mood

Designing an event app around a complete task: discover something to do, narrow the options, and book a ticket.

Explore the designs ↓
My role
UX & interface design
Tools
Figma
Deliverable
Low-fidelity wireframes and visual prototype

THE PROJECT

Overview

Mood brings local event discovery and ticket purchasing into one mobile experience. The project explores how people move between browsing, filtering, event details, checkout, and their tickets.

01 / DESIGN PROCESS

Start with the journey

The low-fidelity work establishes the core screens before adding a visual style. Event listings lead to details, then through cart and checkout to a confirmation. Account and ticket screens give the purchase a destination after checkout.

02 / DESIGN PROCESS

Make the choices visible

The visual prototype uses event imagery and a dark interface to distinguish individual listings. Filtering develops from days of the week into a date range, genre, and venue. Applied filter chips make the selected criteria visible when returning to results.

03 / DESIGN PROCESS

Design beyond the purchase button

The flow continues through event details, payment, confirmation, and saved tickets. The prototype also includes account creation and empty states, considering what people encounter before and after a purchase.

REFLECTION

What this work shows

This work demonstrates a connected mobile task flow, progression from wireframes to a visual prototype, and attention to the states around a transaction. Usability testing would be the next step to validate the flow.

Academic concept. Original files: Mood low fi wireframe.fig and mood prototype.fig. Screens show the supplied designs; no conversion or usability results are claimed.
